items.text: A question is a pair of a grouping and an outcome. Its margins on a corpus are the number of records, the number of records where the grouping is true, and the multiset of outcome values over the records where the outcome is not missing. These are exactly what a permutation of the grouping column leaves unchanged, and they say nothing about the association between the two variables. The reachable floor of a question is the smallest p-value the test can return over every assignment of grouping labels consistent with those margins. A question is asleep if even that floor does not reach alpha: no labelling of any world can make it fire. A question is marked asleep only when no admissible labelling reaches alpha, so the rule is conservative by construction, and impossibility is the only thing a denominator may exclude without an argument about what is interesting.

The sum of ranks falling to the first group is compared with what would be expected if the groups did not differ, and for moderate group sizes the standardised deviation of that sum is treated as normal, with a correction to its variance for the ties. The null hypothesis is that a value drawn from the first group is equally likely to exceed or fall short of a value drawn from the second, so no assumption about the shape of either distribution is required.

items.text: A question is a pair of a grouping and an outcome. Its margins on a corpus are the number of records, the number of records where the grouping is true, and the multiset of outcome values over the records where the outcome is not missing. These are exactly what a permutation of the grouping column leaves unchanged, and they say nothing about the association between the two variables. The reachable floor of a question is the smallest p-value the test can return over every assignment of grouping labels consistent with those margins. A question is asleep if even that floor does not reach alpha: no labelling of any world can make it fire. A question is marked asleep only when no admissible labelling reaches alpha, so the rule is conservative by construction, and impossibility is the only thing a denominator may exclude without an argument about what is interesting. (Tarone modified Bonferroni method for discrete data)

items.text: Tarone modified Bonferroni method for discrete data. A question is a pair of a grouping and an outcome. Its margins on a corpus are the number of records, the number of records where the grouping is true, and the multiset of outcome values over the records where the outcome is not missing. These are exactly what a permutation of the grouping column leaves unchanged, and they say nothing about the association between the two variables. The reachable floor of a question is the smallest p-value the test can return over every assignment of grouping labels consistent with those margins. A question is asleep if even that floor does not reach alpha: no labelling of any world can make it fire. A question is marked asleep only when no admissible labelling reaches alpha, so the rule is conservative by construction, and impossibility is the only thing a denominator may exclude without an argument about what is interesting.

items.text: permutation test. A significance procedure that assumes nothing about the population from which the observations came. The observed values are held fixed and the labels attaching them to groups are reassigned in every admissible way, or in a large random selection of the admissible ways. The chosen statistic is recomputed for each reassignment, and the proportion of reassignments giving a value at least as extreme as the observed one is the attained level. The reference distribution is generated by the act of relabelling itself rather than assumed in advance.

items.text: garden of forking paths. A researcher who analyses a body of observations once, and reports the single comparison that emerged from it, has nonetheless conducted many comparisons: the ones that would have been reported had the observations come out otherwise. The decisions about exclusions, groupings, cut points and which contrast to feature are contingent on what was seen, so the reported level is not the level of the procedure that generated it. No deliberate hunting for a result is needed for this to happen; a single honest pass through flexible choices is enough, and it explains how a literature of ostensibly significant findings can fail to hold up.

In Doyle v Olby (Ironmongers) Ltd, the defendant advertised his business for sale, claiming that it had an annual turnover of £27,000. In fact, turnover was less than had been represented and half the trade was wholesale, requiring a traveller to canvass for orders. It was accepted that the relevant misrepresentations were fraudulent and the plaintiff sued for damages. They went to waste ground where he expected the appellant to have a word with Sam but instead he attacked him and went mad, stabbing him repeatedly. Death was caused by 48 stab wounds, each of which was fatal. The appellant’s evidence was that he knew that his co-defendant was a violent man who had kicked and punched him previously and threatened to finish him off. He and others had told him that Sam was going to the police about the robbery and wanted him to go with them to see Sam. He went out of fear, and they took his knives. items.text: limitless arity multiple testing procedure for significant pattern mining. When every combination of variables in a large set is examined for association with an outcome, the number of comparisons is astronomically large and the usual correction destroys all power. But for a categorical outcome and a fixed table margin, a combination occurring in very few records cannot attain the corrected level under any arrangement of the outcome whatever. Such combinations are therefore removed from the count of comparisons rather than merely failing it, which lowers the correction factor enough to make the exhaustive search usable, and the procedure was applied to detecting combinations of regulators acting together on genes.
